title.value: Quality Indicators and Performance Monitoring in Interventional Pulmonology

key_points: Performance monitoring systematically collects and analyzes metrics to improve bronchoscopy outcomes.
Quality indicators are measurable elements of practice performance linked to patient safety and outcomes.
Indicators fall into structural, process, and outcome measures.
Audit and feedback are critical for reducing variance in care and improving quality.
Large audits and registries (BTS, AQuIRE) have highlighted gaps in quality and informed performance standards.

diagnostic_approaches: Use of quality indicators for bronchoscopy and EBUS performance
Audit and feedback cycles to assess diagnostic sensitivity and complication rates
Standardized reporting of procedural details (indication, sedation, target structures)

definitions.definition: Measurable element of practice performance that acts as a marker of high-quality care.
Indicators assessing healthcare environment and infrastructure.
Indicators assessing delivery of care, often linked to improved outcomes.
Indicators assessing results of care, such as diagnostic sensitivity or complication rates.
Systematic review of performance with feedback to drive improvement.
ACCP multicenter registry collecting bronchoscopy data for quality improvement.

points: Variance in care reflects variability in procedural quality rather than patient factors alone.
Professional responsibility requires all interventional pulmonologists to benchmark outcomes.
Audit and feedback should be a standard feature of IP services aiming for excellence.

quality_indicators.indicator: Consent fully documented incl. risks of EBUS and sedation
Appearance of relevant structures recorded (per indication)
Systematic mediastinal LN staging for ACCP B & C (cN1/2/3)
Diagnostic performance of EBUS-TBNA (by indication/ACCP group)
Specimens inadequate for required molecular testing
